title: Move Intent CI status and timing checks out of Dashboard Integrated UI Test

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-334#retire-dashboard-integrated-ui-test (plan 633, slice 2, obligation G2), revision 7fcfad6772e28f942604f492fdd18d980ec2f218

Verdict: Caught. The assertion that caught it is `expect(ci.reads()).toEqual(firstReads)` at dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-ci-status-kept.spec.ts:127, in test 2, step "time alone and another branch moving ask for no judgment". The claim is limited to the path observed: on the trunk CI homepage, after another watched branch (codex/example-story) moves from f1… to f6…, the faulted page made exactly one extra CI-status judgment read, and that assertion failed on it.

Promise checked: on the trunk CI-status homepage in Intent, time passing and another branch moving do not ask for a new main judgment. A trunk move asks once more. That is Key example 2: "Frontend observes the same values, gaps, freshness cues and keyboard interaction".

Why the suggested fault did not reach the path (and why the earlier break at intentCiTarget.ts:119 stayed green):
- I applied the suggested fault, adding `watchedBranchHeads(work)` to the trunk target's head, and instrumented it. The watched head for codex/example-story stayed `null` on the client before and after the move. In this fixture, the moved branch's plan read at the branch head comes back as `planSlices: {status:"unavailable", problem:"...shape this dashboard does not understand while reading .planning/slice-plans/219-failing/PLAN.md at f1f1…/f6f6…"}`. So `progressSource.head` is never recorded, and the watched-heads map never changes.
- With that fault, the witness counts were {fresh:2,kept:2} both before and after the move. The maintained test passed because the wrong behavior never happened. This explains the implementer's earlier observation: that fault does not reach the path in this fixture.

Revised fault (one edit, fixtures and assertions untouched):
- File: dashboard/src/intentCiTarget.ts, `ciTargetOf`, trunk branch (`selectedIdentity === undefined`).
- Before: `head: work?.revision`
- After: `head: work === undefined ? undefined : \`${work.revision}|${JSON.stringify(work.taken.map((entry) => entry.planSlices))}\``
- Effect: the trunk judgment's followed head changes whenever any taken story's progress is re-read at a moved branch. The page then re-asks the main CI judgment on another branch's movement. This is the only branch-move signal the client work carries in this fixture.
- Another revision I tried and rejected: keying the head to the identity of the work object. It made new work objects on almost every render and re-read endlessly on time alone. That is a different fault, so I reverted it without judging it.

Independent witness (a scratch spec, zz-scratch-witness.spec.ts, with no maintained assertions; deleted afterwards):
- It used the same fixture as test 2 and counted `intent=ci-status` requests with page.on("request").
- After load, untilPageReadsAnswered and two check paces (time alone): ci.reads() = {fresh:3,kept:3}, 6 requests.
- After moving codex/example-story to f6…, then a pace, settle, pace, settle: {fresh:4,kept:4}, 8 requests. That is one extra kept+fresh judgment pair for main, caused only by the other branch moving.
- The fault also adds re-reads while the page first loads progress (3 instead of 1). Those settle before test 2 captures firstReads (the test's firstReads was 3), so they did not cause the catch.
- Reach: in the faulted maintained run, the branch-progress assertion on line 126 (`branchReads > branchReadsBefore`) passed. The page did see the branch move.

Runs (scratch worktree detached at 7fcfad677, npm ci, Node 24.21.0, one worker, host load about 10). The command was `caffeinate -s -i env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run test:dashboard:frontend -- intent/intent-ci-status-kept.spec.ts --workers=1 --reporter=list`.
1. Baseline: 2 passed (8.3s); test 2 took 633ms.
2. Suggested fault plus witness: 3 passed. The fault did not reach the path (no extra reads).
3. Revised fault plus witness: test 1 passed. Test 2 failed at line 127, `expect(ci.reads()).toEqual(firstReads)`, expected {fresh:3,kept:3}, received {fresh:4,kept:4}. The witness passed and showed the extra read.
4. Restored: 2 passed (4.1s).

Restoration: `git checkout dashboard/src/intentCiTarget.ts` and the witness spec deleted. `git status --porcelain` was empty, with HEAD at 7fcfad6772e28f942604f492fdd18d980ec2f218, the same as the clean state before the probe. The restored focused run passed (2 passed). The scratch worktree was removed and no longer appears in `git worktree list`. No edits were made to the execution checkout.

Next proof action: none is needed for this promise, since the maintained assertion catches a page that re-reads the trunk judgment when another branch moves. Optional, for the caller to decide: the fixture's moved-branch plan read fails to parse ("shape this dashboard does not understand"). So test 2 shows the branch move only through a failed progress re-read, never through a recorded branch head. A fault keyed to watched branch heads (like the one at intentCiTarget.ts:119) cannot reach the path until the fixture gives a well-formed plan read at the branch head. If the caller wants that variant covered, the next action is to make the substitute answer that read in a shape the page understands, then repeat this probe with the watched-heads fault.

Prior disposition: this matches the implementer's note that the intentCiTarget.ts:119 break "never reached the code path". The probe confirms that diagnosis and attributes it to the fixture's unparsed plan read. That is recognition of the earlier note, not a new repair decision.

Cost:
- Test runtime: measured, from Playwright's reported wall time. Baseline 8.3s, faulted runs about 5.8s, 3.4–4.0s and 8.2s (several runs included the witness), restored 4.1s. About 34s in total across the 6 runs.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part during the probe, and there is no separate measure.
- Agent effort: unavailable as a separately supported measure. No token or tool-time count was available to this agent. There were about 15 tool calls; this is an estimate by count, not a cost.

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 208062 ms (measured), from 1794756868000 to 1794757076062 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision 7fcfad6772e28f942604f492fdd18d980ec2f218: Caught; no follow-up. The optional fixture variant (well-formed plan read at a moved branch head) is not needed for this promise.
